title: What is Grok Bot?
summary: Grok Bot is SpaceXSI's app for building a team of AI agents that run routines in the cloud. Here's how it works, what it costs, and where it falls short.
body_markdown:
Working with AI is getting weird. Two years ago, I used to do most tasks by myself and then jump into a chatbot task to solve a problem four or five times per hour. These days, I end up staring at my screen while my agents do my research, tear down my drafts, or fix up formatting—mostly to make sure they're not going off-task. Is that what we're supposed to be, now? Glorified babysitters to thinking machines?


Grok Bot is SpaceX Super Intelligence's solution to this problem. Instead of a chatbot that you have to manage and wait on, you set up a team of agents that work on routines, message each other to hand off work, and only tug at your sleeve when it matters.

## What is Grok Bot?


Grok Bot is an[AI agent app](https://zapier.com/blog/best-ai-agents/) by SpaceXSI, where you create a team of Bots, each with its own name, role, and context. They share a persistent cloud computer with a browser, file system, and terminal. Using these tools, they can work on multi-step tasks in real websites, message each other to hand off work, and will keep running even when your laptop is off.


In[ChatGPT](https://zapier.com/blog/how-to-use-chatgpt/) or[Claude](https://zapier.com/blog/claude-ai/) , your chats pile up in history, each starting from nearly zero context. In Grok Bot, each chat is tied to an AI teammate, similar to a contact list on a messaging app. Whenever you want to take care of your inbox, you open your email Bot and tackle your unread messages; if you're researching a competitor, that's a task for your Investigator Bot. The experience feels more fluid because it's how you work with real people.


Each Bot keeps its memory, files, browser data, and preferences across sessions. The workflow's context builds over time; in a regular chatbot, you'd have to build it nearly from scratch in every new session. You can also teach your Bots how to do things by either describing the task in text or taking over the remote computer to record the workflow.


And since Bots can collaborate with one another and participate in group chats, you can control multiple chat threads at the same time. You don't have to break your workflow across two or three threads and feed each as the output comes back. This makes interacting with AI less cognitively taxing, as you spend less time context-switching; the bots feed you, not the other way around.


Grok Bot is a great fit for people drowning in admin work and who need to automate complex tasks in apps or websites that don't have an integration or a connector yet.


## How to get started with Grok Bot


Grok Bot is available as an app download for Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android. Here's how to get everything ready:


1.


Head to the[official website](https://x.ai/bot) .


2.


Click the download button, and install the Grok Bot app.


3.


Sign up or log in to your account, and go through the onboarding steps.


4.


Activate the trial or link your account to Cursor/SuperGrok/X Premium+. Activating the trial requires providing your credit card details, but you won't be charged until you decide to upgrade.


5.


Finish logging in to Grok Bot, and start the app's onboarding flow.


Let me take you on a guided tour. Keep the app open as you read through the next sections, and configure the app the way you want it to work at each step.


## How does Grok Bot work?


The first time you land on your workspace, your main Grok Bot comes out to greet you. It handles the onboarding process, helping you understand what makes it different from a chatbot. After the brief intro, it dives right into creating other Bots based on the work that you usually do.


### Bots and their cloud computer


Use the main Grok Bot interview to create your first few Bots, and then dip into each new chat window to configure behaviors and instructions. This is all done in a conversation, not a visual workflow builder.


Your Bots all stack on the left side of the screen. Think of these like contacts. You can come back to each thread at any time to continue the conversation or ask to start a new task.


When you click the Bot's name badge, notice the *Computer* tab on the right side. This is your access point to the remote computer that all your Bots share. When your Bot is performing a complex task like booking a flight, you can open the computer and see where it currently is in that process. It's a barebones machine: it comes with a Chrome browser, a simple file manager, and a terminal. You can take it over and use it at any time to unblock a workflow.


### Teach a Bot with a workflow recording


While viewing the remote computer, you can click the record button at the top right to teach a Bot how to complete a task. Once you stop, the Bot will view the video and convert what you did into text-based instructions it can reuse later.


There's another entry point for teaching your Bots: click the plus icon on the prompt window, and select **Teach a task** . This takes you directly to the remote computer so you can start recording your workflow there.


### Connectors


Connectors plug a Bot straight into your apps, like Gmail for your inbox or Granola for your meetings. There are dozens of connectors available: you can browse them by clicking **Connect apps** at the bottom left of the screen.


These connectors are[MCP servers](https://zapier.com/blog/mcp/) that Grok Bot uses to get information or control external apps. For tasks that have no connector, your Bot relies on the virtual computer instead.


Once you connect an external app, you can open it on the Marketplace to adjust permissions. For example, after connecting Gmail, you can expand the tools section to reveal all the actions and selectively enable or disable them based on your needs. This is useful for blocking email sending if you only want Grok Bot to draft messages for you, for example.


Grok also[connects with Zapier](https://zapier.com/blog/automate-grok/) , allowing it to securely access and take action across 9,000+


apps. With one install, you can let Grok work with all your apps, and it's all governed through Zapier.


[Automate Grok Bot](https://zapier.com/apps/ai-tools/grok-bot)


### Teams of Bots


Here's where things get fun. If you want to send a task from one Bot to another, you can do it via the chat: in my tests, I asked the Researcher Bot to get a new topic from the Topic Scout. The Researcher texted Topic Scout on its own, picked one of the three topics that it received back, and started researching it right away. I went back to Topic Scout and saw a brief acknowledgment of the interaction, which is great for tracking what's happening.


If you end up with multiple Bots in a single workflow or project, you can create a group chat instead of relying on 1-to-1 messaging. You still control the direction of the work with prompts, and the Bots will collaborate, mention each other, and delegate tasks based on their roles to achieve your objective.


### Routines


A big part of automating work is having it happen on a schedule without your direct intervention—otherwise, you're back to babysitting. Bots support routines, which can run at any interval, such as every morning or every two hours. Once you set your instructions and set up your connectors, you can delegate tasks like[email triage](https://zapier.com/blog/best-ai-email-assistant/) or keeping tabs on a trend automatically.


Also, since your Bots are in the cloud, they run even if your laptop is closed. Work doesn't stop even if you're sleeping or on holiday.


### Approvals


Not every action gets an approval notification, which cuts both ways. Too many approval notifications means the Bots will always be bothering you to do their work; not enough can keep a Bot working after it's gone astray.


The email connector has a good balance here, showing a preview window with the message. If it looks good, you can send it right away; if not, it's easy to cancel and ask for changes. The process is similar for trashing emails, which makes sense for this type of destructive action.


But when I connected Google Docs, I didn't get pinged for approval on anything. The Bots did exactly what I asked for, but I was left wondering what could've happened if they didn't.


There are two ways to control this. The first one is by enabling/disabling tool actions as we've explored before. The other is:


1.


Head to **Settings** (bottom left menu).


2.


Scroll down to the *Bot* section.


3.


In the input labeled "When Grok Bot wants to," write a prompt of the action you want to control, such as "Making edits to Google Docs documents."


4.


Select whether it should allow automatically or ask first.


5.


Click **Add rule** to save.


### Put the Bots in your pocket


Your Grok Bots work in the cloud and are accessible via the mobile app for iOS and Android. This is one of the best ways to keep tabs on your work as you go about your day, especially if a part of it involves being away from your laptop. You can use it to see what's new or start new actions.


## What can you use Grok Bot for?


After building my own daily AI News Briefing Bot and research team, I went out to read how other people were using Grok Bot to get work done.


### Daily admin and inbox triage


The pain: keeping tabs on email, Slack, your calendar, and important docs while you're trying to maintain focus.[SpaceXSI's work guide](https://x.ai/bot/guides/grok-bot-for-work) splits this across four Bots:


-


An Inbox Manager that connects to your communication channels, prioritizing important messages and letting the noise sink to the bottom.


-


A Calendar EA that keeps an eye on your time, batching meetings together and finding focus blocks.


-


An Intel Scout to keep track of major changes in projects, so you're not caught by surprise.


-


A Bot Boss that you message directly, acting as a single point of contact so you can manage your day in one place instead of three.


Creator Jerad Hill[runs a similar setup](https://jeradhill.substack.com/p/how-i-stopped-being-the-go-between) for inbox monitoring. A brand deal Bot screens emails for sponsorship deals, surfacing and drafting replies for each offer. He says that it found over $4,000 that would have otherwise landed in the trash.


### Invoices and expenses


No one loves chasing expenses and invoices. Create an Invoice Hunter like the builders at[AI Maker did](https://aimaker.substack.com/p/grok-bot-ai-agent-team) , connect it to Gmail and Google Drive, and tell it to grab everything into a new Google Sheets file. Instead of combing through your inbox, you get everything neatly organized in a spreadsheet, ready to go over whenever you're ready.


### Support triage


Watching a customer support ticket queue isn't the best use of your time. SpaceXSI[set their Grok Bots on the task](https://x.ai/bot/guides/grok-bot-for-support) , working on top of each request to reproduce reported bugs, analyze churn, or decide on whether to provide refunds.


And this just lifts the lid on many possibilities across sales, recruiting, engineering, and more.


## Grok Bot pricing: How much does Grok Bot cost?


Hop on the free trial to get a taste of how Grok Bot works. You need to add your credit card details to unlock it, but it doesn't charge you anything until you decide to upgrade. The allowance is good enough for trying out a few tasks, but in my experience, it dries up easily in about an hour of sustained use.


If you liked the taster and want more, Grok Bot doesn't have its own individual pricing: it's bundled with Cursor Pro, Cursor Teams, some SuperGrok plans, and the X Premium+ plan. It's not included with SuperGrok Lite, Team, and Enterprise.

## Grok Bot's limitations


Grok Bot is still pretty new, and it has a lot of potential, a few rough edges, and not a ton of clarity around the mechanics of some features. Here are a few things to keep in mind.


**Long chats can get expensive fast.** Every time a Bot replies on its main thread, it re-reads the entire conversation context, burning a lot of usage. Multiply this by half a dozen Bots running on autopilot weeks on end, and you can hit your plan ceiling quickly—or, worse, run into overages if you have pay-as-you-go activated.


There's a workaround. Instead of continuing every chat in each Bot's main window:


1.


Click the plus button at the top left.


2.


Start a new conversation with one of your existing Bots.


3.


Add your instructions there.


Alternatively, you can tell your Bots to stop texting one another or space out hourly routines.


**Messaging a Bot in the middle of the task can make it start over** . I was trying to book a flight to Canada to see how it handled using real web interfaces, and I made the mistake of sending a prompt before it was finished. The Bot went back to step 1.


**CAPTCHAs, payments, and logins still need you.** CAPTCHAs are anti-bot protections that Grok can't quite manage on its own. Payments are a sensitive action, so it makes sense that they should require your green light. And if the Bot doesn't have the login credentials at hand, it can't use your accounts, so be ready to provide them if your workflow needs it.


**Bots share the same virtual machine, so there's no isolation.** You can't keep context separate or add security boundaries, which could lower precision when taking actions or leak information.


**Is the virtual machine safe?** I can't confidently say yet. The current docs don't offer a thorough answer, but it's worth thinking about. If your Bot visits a malicious website and triggers a harmful script there, does the virtual machine get infected? Can it take over your agents to leak your data? This isn't unique to Grok Bot, but it's worth considering before you give your Bots free rein.


## Grok Bot competitors and alternatives


Grok Bot falls into the[autonomous agent](https://zapier.com/blog/types-of-ai-agents/) category, lowering the cost and setup curve compared with two earlier releases:


-


[OpenClaw](https://zapier.com/blog/openclaw/) , the original autonomous agent framework that went viral in January 2026. It's open-source, self-hostable, and runs on your own hardware. It works based on instructions you send via popular messaging apps, but it quickly got dinged for potential security issues.


-


[Hermes Agent](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/) is an OpenClaw alternative created by Nous Research and released in February 2026.


But the competition in the space increases as Meta and OpenAI, among others, have all launched their own takes on easy-to-use autonomous agents:


-


[Meta Muse](https://zapier.com/blog/muse-ai/) launched in September 2026, and it works on desktop, mobile, or as a contact in WhatsApp. There's even hardware on the roadmap, trying to[surf the Tamagotchi wave](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/23/meta-made-a-tamagotchi-like-wearable-for-its-muse-ai-agent/) .


-


[ChatGPT dots](https://openai.com/index/introducing-dots/) also launched in September 2026. It was announced at OpenAI DevDay and is very similar to the rest in terms of functionality.


With nearly all the major players releasing their take on what an autonomous agent should be, it's the perfect time to try them and see how they fit the way you work.


## Connect Grok Bot to Zapier


If there's no connector for an app you use for work, your agent will try to make it happen in the virtual computer, but it's pretty clunky. Instead, use the Zapier connector, and your Bots will get secure access to 9,000+


apps. You decide which apps and actions it's allowed to touch, and it's all taken care of with one install.


The connection works like a regular[MCP connection](https://zapier.com/blog/zapier-mcp-guide/) :


1.


Click the **Connect apps** button at the bottom left.


2.


Search for Zapier in the search bar.


3.


Click to add the connector, log in to Zapier, and authorize Cursor (Grok Bot).


4.


Go into a Bot chat and run` /zapier-setup` to discover and connect available actions.


Once connected, you can use both the Zaps you already have configured, as well as all actions that Zapier has available for a given app.


[Try Zapier](https://zapier.com/)


## The Bot-tom line


AI promises to give you back time by automating tasks, but sometimes takes it away with long configuration processes or by forcing you to monitor everything. Grok Bot is another step in the time-saving direction: it's so easy to set up and use that you can go back to the work that only you can do.


A final note on Grok models and SpaceXSI: there's been wide media coverage on how Grok models have been used for generating deepfakes and propagating political messages. During my testing, I didn't find that the model produced harmful outputs that could be detrimental to someone doing regular work. But that's just my experience: if it's something that concerns you, pick one of the alternatives instead.
